Series::invalid_index¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::invalid_index() const -> Series

What It Does¶

invalid_index() compresses the same diagnosis as invalid() into a 1D int64 list of flat positions.

The positions are row-major flattened indices into self.

That matters because the result is no longer mask-shaped like the original Series; it is compact. If only three lanes are invalid, the result contains only three index values.

That compact form is useful in two different directions:

  • as a getter input for methods like take(), where the goal is to retrieve just the invalid values

  • as a setter input for methods like put_(), where the goal is to replace exactly those invalid positions

Parameters¶

None.

Returns¶

Series A 1D int64 Series containing the flat positions of every invalid lane.

Gradient¶

invalid_index() is index discovery, not a differentiable numeric transform.

Examples¶

Example 1. The returned indices are flattened positions, not 2D coordinate pairs.

auto values = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 2.0},
    {std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     5.0},
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, values.invalid_index());

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 3, 4]

In that 2 x 3 example, the flattened positions are:

  • position 1 -> (0, 1) -> nan

  • position 3 -> (1, 0) -> +inf

  • position 4 -> (1, 1) -> -inf

Example 2. Those same indices can be used immediately as a getter. take() reads flat positions from the original Series and returns only the invalid lanes.

auto values = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 2.0},
    {std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     5.0},
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, values.take(values.invalid_index()));

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[nan, inf, -inf]

This is the compact getter pattern:

  • invalid() tells you where the bad lanes are as a full mask

  • invalid_index() compresses that diagnosis into flat positions

  • take(...) uses those positions to fetch just the bad values

Example 3. For in-place constant repair, the cleanest surface is usually the shape-preserving boolean mask from invalid().

auto values = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 2.0},
    {std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     5.0},
});

values.where_(values.invalid(), -99.0);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, values);

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡   1.0000 -99.0000 2.0000 ⎤
⎣ -99.0000 -99.0000 5.0000 ⎦

Use that route when the replacement policy is one scalar value or one broadcastable branch. The mask keeps the original shape, so the call reads very directly: “where invalid, write -99.0.”

Example 4. For positional replacement with one value per invalid lane, invalid_index() pairs naturally with put_().

auto values = pluss::make_series({
    {1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(), 2.0},
    {std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
     5.0},
});

values.put_(values.invalid_index(), pluss::make_series({70.0, 80.0, 90.0}));
std::cout << values;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2,3], strides=[3,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=6, contiguous=true)
data=[[1, 70, 2],
  [80, 90, 5]]

This is the array-valued setter pattern:

  • invalid_index() returns exactly three positions here

  • the replacement Series therefore must provide exactly three values unless a scalar broadcast is intended

  • the write still lands back into the original 2 x 3 layout even though the index list itself is flat

There is not yet a dedicated callback-style “fill invalid lanes by function” method on the public Series surface. The current general pattern is to build the replacement Series first, using whatever deterministic rule is needed, and then write it back with put_().

Example 5. If nothing is invalid, the result is an empty 1D index list.

pluss::series::print(std::cout, pluss::make_series({1.5, 2.5, 3.5}).invalid_index());

Output¶

Series(shape=[0], strides=[1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=0, contiguous=true)
[]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • These are flat row-major positions, not per-axis coordinate rows.

  • The result is compact, so its size depends on how many invalid lanes were found, not on the shape of self.

  • For shape-preserving replacement, the boolean-mask route via invalid() and where_() is often simpler than a flat index write.

  • For per-invalid replacement values, put_() expects either one scalar source value or a source with one lane per returned invalid index.

  • If you need a same-shape boolean answer for branching or masking, use invalid() instead.

Summary¶

Use invalid_index() when the important result is the compact list of bad positions, especially if the next step is “fetch those exact lanes” or “overwrite those exact lanes.”

See Also¶

  • Series::invalid: same diagnosis, but shape-preserving.

  • Series::nonzero: general truthy-position extractor.

  • Series::take: consume flat positions against flattened storage.

  • Series::put_: overwrite flat positions in place.

  • Series::where_: shape-preserving masked in-place replacement.
